chapters.name: Matrices and Determinants
chapters.introduction: Matrices represent data in rows and columns. Determinants are scalar values derived from square matrices. SEE covers order, operations, inverse, and determinant of 2×2 matrices.
chapters.whyItMatters: 12-15 marks. Matrix operations and inverse are always tested.

topics.name: Matrix Operations
topics.explanation: For 2×2 matrices A and B: Addition/Subtraction requires same order. Multiplication: (2×2)(2×2) → (2×2). Scalar multiplication multiplies every element. Transpose swaps rows and columns.
topics.examTip: Always check dimensions are compatible before multiplying.
topics.formula:
For A = [[a,b],[c,d]]:  det(A) = ad - bc
A⁻¹ = (1/det(A)) × [[d,-b],[-c,a]]

topics.name: Complex Numbers
topics.explanation: Complex number z = a + bi, where a is real part and b is imaginary part. i = √(-1), i² = -1. Operations: addition (add real and imaginary separately), multiplication (use FOIL), modulus |z| = √(a²+b²).

chapters.name: Straight Line and Curves
chapters.introduction: Covers equation of straight lines (all forms), pair of straight lines, circle, parabola basics, and distance/area formulas.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Straight line problems are the highest-weighted coordinate geometry section.

topics.name: Straight Lines
topics.explanation: Forms: Slope-intercept y = mx+c; Point-slope y-y₁ = m(x-x₁); Two-point (y-y₁)/(y₂-y₁) = (x-x₁)/(x₂-x₁). Parallel lines: equal slopes. Perpendicular lines: m₁×m₂ = -1.
topics.examTip: Convert to slope-intercept form first to read the slope directly.
topics.formula: y = mx + c  ;  m = tan θ  ;  Distance = |c₁-c₂|/√(1+m²)

chapters.name: Advanced Trigonometric Identities
chapters.introduction: Compound angle formulas, double angle formulas, product-to-sum and sum-to-product formulas, and solving trigonometric equations.
chapters.whyItMatters: 15-18 marks. Identity proofs and graph sketching are standard Optional Math questions.

topics.name: Compound Angle Formulas
topics.explanation: sin(A±B) = sinA cosB ± cosA sinB. cos(A±B) = cosA cosB ∓ sinA sinB. Double angle: sin 2A = 2 sinA cosA, cos 2A = cos²A - sin²A = 1 - 2sin²A = 2cos²A - 1.
keyPoints: Derive double angle from compound angle (A=B)
topics.examTip: Start proof from the more complex side. Never cross-multiply.
topics.formula:
sin(A+B) = sinAcosB + cosAsinB
cos(A+B) = cosAcosB - sinAsinB
sin2A = 2sinAcosA

chapters.name: Limits and Derivatives
chapters.introduction: Introduction to limits, continuity, and differentiation. Covers power rule, product rule, quotient rule, and chain rule for polynomials and trigonometric functions.
chapters.whyItMatters: 12-15 marks. Differentiation rules are directly tested with polynomial and trig functions.

topics.name: Derivatives
topics.explanation: Power rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹. Product rule: d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv'. Quotient rule: d/dx(u/v) = (u'v - uv')/v². Chain rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x))·g'(x). Common: d/dx(sinx)=cosx, d/dx(cosx)=-sinx.
keyPoints: Power rule is the most used
topics.examTip: For complex functions, identify the form (product/quotient/chain) before applying the rule.
